architecture.title: A local-first decision service: extract, decide, and keep the data boundary in code
architecture.caption: One question set, three engines. An adapter turns Jev's choice/noul/score questions into each engine's input. Classic GLiNER finds spans with offsets; a decision model picks among them. pick_engine() in code decides where text may go: confidential text stays on local engines (Laya, GLiNER2.5-Decide), everything else can use hosted Jev. Low-confidence local answers go to a person, never quietly to the cloud.

sequence.title: Lab 16-3 — GLiNER finds the rooms, Jev picks the one with the problem
sequence.caption: Measured on 2026-10-17. GLiNER (local, ~6 s to load, then milliseconds) marks two room numbers in the Thai ticket — one is really FLOOR 3. Jev's Choice over the candidates picks room 1203 (0.92). Code keeps the offsets and highlights the span.

charts.caption: labs/lab05_bakeoff.py on 2026-10-17, zero-shot, 12 English + 6 Thai synthetic tickets. A classroom sample, not a verdict — but it agrees in direction with the independent Jev Decision Index (Jev 60.11, Decide 9.24, Laya 4.43).
